ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and the three vertices of a triangle are all on the circle. The base of the triangle is labeled 8 cm, the right vertical side is labeled 15 cm, and there is a right-angle mark between the base and the right vertical side. The hypotenuse connects the lower-left vertex and the upper vertex, and passes through the center marked inside the circle. Reasoning: Because the hypotenuse passes through the center and both endpoints are on the circle, this hypotenuse is the diameter of the circle. The triangle is a right triangle, with legs 8 and 15 respectively, so the diameter d = sqrt(8^2 + 15^2) = sqrt(64 + 225) = sqrt(289) = 17. The circumference of the circle C = πd = 17π.

raw_record.question_text: The triangle is inscribed into the circle. Find the exact circumference of the circle.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as an inscribed right triangle: the bottom horizontal side is labeled 8 cm, the right vertical side is labeled 15 cm, and the pink square marks the angle between them as 90°. The slanted side connects the other two vertices and passes through the marked circle center, so it is the circle’s diameter. Apply the Pythagorean theorem to the right triangle: diameter = sqrt(8^2 + 15^2) = sqrt(64 + 225) = 17. Then use the circumference formula C = pi*d to get C = 17π.
